checks.method: read the full header and source diff; confirmed every deleted header line is a private constructor declaration or a documentation comment; grepped src/xverse/xcom and tests/xcom for RouteSpec equality/near-equality use, route_snapshot, policy_bound, and route_policy consumers

checks.name: Declared-policy binding semantics: explicit, bounded, immutable, no substitution, no silent upgrade
checks.method: read RouteSpec::policy_, has_policy(), policy(), create_impl, the four-argument factory, the private RouteSpec constructor, LifecycleSnapshot::policy_bound, and LifecycleController::route_policy; cross-checked detailed-design.md sections 4.1-4.3 and requirements.md T014-SR-007..-010; read the four new unit cases and three new negative cases
checks.result: pass: a route either declares exactly one already-validated FlowPolicy, copied through policy_.emplace(*policy), or none. policy() returns nullptr and route_policy returns a stable failure for an unbound generation, so no default is substituted. At most one FlowPolicy is stored per RouteSpec and per route record (std::optional), so the binding is bounded and the declared policy is not reinterpreted as lifecycle capacity. No public operation rebinds, replaces, weakens, or strengthens a live generation's declared policy; the only change path is close plus recreation as a strictly higher generation, after which the earlier handle's route_policy fails invalid_handle. The generation value is only advanced after a successful declaration, so a rejected declaration cannot consume or reuse a generation.

checks.name: Exact handle authentication, fail-closed diagnostics, and rejected-operation atomicity
checks.method: read authenticate_route (both overloads), route_policy, and the invalid_handle/failure helpers; read test_route_policy_handle_boundaries, test_route_policy_absent_diagnostic, and test_policy_bound_route_compatibility_unchanged; re-ran the lifecycle CTest executables
checks.result: pass: route_policy is const, takes the single internal std::mutex via lock_guard, and calls authenticate_route, which accepts a handle only when controller identity, resource kind, logical identity, plan digest, and generation all equal a current record. A stale, foreign, wrong-kind, or mismatched handle yields exactly one ownership-phase XCOM-LIFE-E009 diagnostic; a generation that declared no policy yields exactly one route_declaration-phase XCOM-TYPE-E001 diagnostic. Neither path mutates a record. The negative suite compares fresh route snapshots before and after the absent-policy read, the foreign-handle read, and the policy-bound activation rejection, so the no-side-effect property is asserted rather than assumed.

Non-blocking observation (no correction required for this task, surface for the deferred external review): in tests/xcom/endpoint_route_lifecycle/unit_tests.cpp the case `test_route_policy_immutability` states `routes differing only by declared policy compared equal` but constructs its two compared routes with different logical identities (`policy_route("route.a", ...)` versus `policy_route("route.b", ...)`). The inequality assertion therefore holds on identity alone and would not by itself detect a regression in which RouteSpec's defaulted operator== stopped comparing the declared policy. The required property is still guaranteed by construction (RouteSpec's `= default` comparison compares every non-static member, including the optional declared policy) and is covered operationally by the additivity check T014-RV-03 and the recreation case in `test_route_policy_generation_binding`, so the property is verified; the assertion could be strengthened in a later task (T016's consolidated matrix owns cross-cutting policy/equality coverage) by comparing two same-identity routes that differ only in policy. Recorded as a note rather than a finding because production behaviour is correct and the requirement is independently established.

Public-safety convention observed and accepted: the workflow's own deterministic-gate tool path appears in verification-plan.md and implementation.md. It is the workflow tool path (not a credential, private address, payload, or sensitive deployment value) and is used identically in the accepted T007-T013 work products; it is recorded rather than treated as a blocking finding under T014-SR-019.

Context isolation: this is a repository-owned internal read-only review executed on the same host toolchain as the implementation work, not an external or independent-organization review; it claims no external independence, no runtime/production readiness, and no user acceptance.
